_doc: Seasons on the street map (world/streetSeasons.js, world/innerMap/streetSeasons.js, ui/innerMapLayers/streetSeasons.js). The ground's state is worked out day by day from the weather's own precipitation field and a smooth seasonal temperature: snow piles up on cold wet days and melts on warm ones (slush, then mud), ponds and rivers freeze over in a hard winter and go thin again near the thaw, rain softens the unpaved ground into mud, and autumn leaves fall and lie. Nothing here draws randomness: it is a pure function of the world, the hex and the day.

temperature._doc: Celsius = (tile.temperature + curve + climate era + daily wobble) * 80 - 30. The curve is a cosine through the year, coldest on `coldestDay` of the year (1-120).

snow._doc: Precipitation over `wetAbove` falls as snow below `snowBelowC`; it melts by `meltPerDegree` a warm day (rain melts `rainMelt` more). Depth 0..1.

ice._doc: Freezing degree-days build ice (its thickness 0..max); warm ones eat it. Ponds and lakes are walkable at `solid`; rivers (running water) count only `riverRate` of the ice. Under `thin` (or while thawing under `rottenBelow`) the ice is thin and may crack under the player: each step on it `crackBase` x (1 - strength). The sea never freezes on the street map.

mud._doc: Rain on soft ground (precipitation over `wetAbove`, above freezing) wets it; dry days dry it; snowmelt soaks it. Mud 0..1 on unpaved roads, trodden soil, bare earth and fields.

leaves._doc: Leaves lie by the day of the year: [day, density 0..1] points, interpolated (autumn days 61-90; the first days of winter they rot and blow away).

pace._doc: How fast feet (and carts, the second number) go over the ground: x speed. Deep snow off the cleared streets drags (scaled by the snow's depth), mud on soft ground (scaled by the mud), slush and ice a little.

harvestFair._doc: Every town (not a camp) keeps a harvest fair a few days in autumn, its first day `firstDay` plus a hash of the town up to `spread` (days of the season, 1-30); a great fair on (systems/marketFairs.js) counts too. Stalls, produce and bunting go up on the square, the town comes out, a fiddler plays.
lines: Three for a penny, the apples!
Best harvest in years, they say.
Look at the size of that marrow!

midwinter._doc: The longest nights: a great bonfire on the square `days` of winter (days of the season), lit from `hours[0]` till `hours[1]`; folk gather round it.
lines: Midwinter! The days grow longer now.

shovelling._doc: After snow, of a morning, folk clear the street by their door (the street stays clear: snow banks either side).
lines: That's the path clear, at least.

snowPlay._doc: Children out in the snow: snowmen and snowballs. A few snowmen stand about the square while the snow lasts.

sowing._doc: Spring: folk out working the fields round town, sowing and breaking the soil, these days of spring (1-30); `extra` is the added chance a working hand goes out to the fields.

thinIce: The ice groans underfoot. It's thin here.
crack: The ice cracks and you plunge into the freezing water!
fair: {town} keeps its harvest fair: stalls on the square, music and dancing.
midwinter: {town} lights its midwinter bonfire on the square tonight.
frozen: The water here is frozen hard enough to walk on.
mud: The rain has turned the unpaved ground to mud: slow going on foot and for carts.
